description: Test whether the AATK qPCR primers of PMID:35902728 (Table S1) are human-specific by aligning them to human NM_004920 / NM_001080395 and mouse NM_007377 / BC080846, and quote how the paper verified AATK overexpression
code:
import requests, re, time
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

E = "https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/efetch.fcgi"

def fasta(acc, db="nuccore"):
    r = requests.get(E, params={"db": db, "id": acc, "rettype": "fasta", "retmode": "text"}, timeout=120)
    time.sleep(0.4)
    lines = r.text.strip().split("\n")
    return lines[0], "".join(l.strip() for l in lines[1:])

def rc(s):
    return s.translate(str.maketrans("ACGTacgt", "TGCAtgca"))[::-1]

# primers from Woods et al. 2022 Supplementary Table S1 (AATK qPCR pair)
F = "TGGCCTGGCTCACTGCAAGTACAG"
R = "CCCAGATGGTCACGCCCAGG"

targets = ["NM_004920", "NM_001080395", "NM_007377", "BC080846", "NM_001198787"]
seqs = {}
for a in targets:
    h, s = fasta(a)
    seqs[a] = s
    print(f"{a:15s} {len(s):6d} nt  {h[:80]}")

def best_match(primer, seq):
    """exact scan first; otherwise sliding-window minimum Hamming distance"""
    L = len(primer)
    best = (10**6, -1)
    for i in range(len(seq) - L + 1):
        w = seq[i:i+L]
        mm = sum(1 for a, b in zip(primer, w) if a != b)
        if mm < best[0]:
            best = (mm, i)
            if mm == 0:
                break
    return best

rows = []
print("\nprimer alignment (mismatches / primer length, 0-based start, strand)")
for a in targets:
    s = seqs[a].upper()
    fmm, fpos = best_match(F, s)
    rmm, rpos = best_match(rc(R), s)          # reverse primer matches reverse-complement on plus strand
    amp = (rpos + len(R) - fpos) if (fpos >= 0 and rpos > fpos) else None
    rows.append((a, fmm, fpos, rmm, rpos, amp))
    print(f"{a:15s} F {fmm}/{len(F)} @ {fpos:6d}   R {rmm}/{len(R)} @ {rpos:6d}   amplicon {amp}")

# show the actual mouse windows to make the mismatches visible
for a in ["NM_007377", "BC080846"]:
    s = seqs[a].upper()
    fmm, fpos = best_match(F, s)
    rmm, rpos = best_match(rc(R), s)
    print(f"\n{a} forward-primer best window:")
    print("  primer :", F)
    print("  target :", s[fpos:fpos+len(F)])
    print("  diffs  :", "".join(" " if x == y else "^" for x, y in zip(F, s[fpos:fpos+len(F)])))
    print(f"{a} reverse-primer best window (as revcomp on plus strand):")
    print("  primer :", rc(R))
    print("  target :", s[rpos:rpos+len(R)])
    print("  diffs  :", "".join(" " if x == y else "^" for x, y in zip(rc(R), s[rpos:rpos+len(R)])))

# ---- figure: mismatch counts ----
labels = [r[0] for r in rows]
fmms = [r[1] for r in rows]
rmms = [r[3] for r in rows]
x = range(len(labels))
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4.2))
ax.bar([i - 0.19 for i in x], fmms, width=0.38, label="forward primer (24 nt)", color="#3b6ea5")
ax.bar([i + 0.19 for i in x], rmms, width=0.38, label="reverse primer (20 nt)", color="#c06c3e")
ax.set_xticks(list(x))
ax.set_xticklabels(["NM_004920\nhuman 1271 aa", "NM_001080395\nhuman 1374 aa",
                    "NM_007377\nmouse", "BC080846\nmouse clone", "NM_001198787\nmouse"], fontsize=8)
ax.set_ylabel("mismatches in best window")
ax.set_title("AATK qPCR primers of PMID:35902728 against human and mouse transcripts", fontsize=10)
ax.legend(fontsize=8)
ax.axhline(0, color="k", lw=0.8)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
